\lean{FABL.mean_signRestriction_sub_mean_eq_sum_nonempty}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p037-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p147-b003,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p212-b004,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p212-b005,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p213-b001
}
\label{FABL.mean_signRestriction_sub_mean_eq_sum_nonempty}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.expect_eq_indexedFourierCoeff_empty, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.indexedMonomial, FABL.liftFixedFrequency, FABL.liftFreeFrequency, FABL.mean, FABL.mean_eq_fourierCoeff_empty, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff, FABL.restrictionFourierCoeff_eq_sum, FABL.signRestriction}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $f$ be a real-valued function on the sign cube
$\\{−1,1\\}^n$, let $J\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$, and fix signs $z_i\in\{−1,1\}$ for
$i\notin J$. The mean of $f$ over the cube with these fixed signs, minus its mean over
the full cube, equals the sum over all nonempty subsets $T\subseteq J^c$ of the Fourier
coefficient of $f$ at $T$, multiplied by $\prod_{i\in T}z_i$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Mean change under a sign restriction]
\lean{FABL.IsLowDegreeFourierRegular.abs_mean_signRestriction_sub_mean_le}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p146-b006,
  pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p147-b003
}
\label{FABL.IsLowDegreeFourierRegular.abs_mean_signRestriction_sub_mean_le}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.IsLowDegreeFourierRegular, FABL.fourierCoeff, FABL.indexedMonomial, FABL.indexedMonomial_sq, FABL.liftFixedFrequency, FABL.mean, FABL.mean_signRestriction_sub_mean_eq_sum_nonempty, FABL.signRestriction}
\difficulty{5}
Let $n,k$ be nonnegative integers, let $f:\\{-1,1\\}^n\\to\\mathbb R$ be Fourier-regular
at level $k$ with bound $\\varepsilon\\ge0$, let $J\\subseteq\\{1,\\ldots,n\\}$, and fix
signs on the coordinates outside $J$. If the number of coordinates outside $J$ is at
most $k$, then the absolute difference between the mean of the resulting restriction of
$f$ (averaged over the free coordinates in $J$) and the mean of $f$ on the full cube is
at most $2^k\\varepsilon$.
\end{theorem}

\difficulty{6}
Let $f$ be a real-valued function on the $n$-dimensional sign cube, and suppose it is
not Fourier-regular at degree at most $k$ with tolerance $\varepsilon$; that is, some
nonempty set of coordinates of size at most $k$ has a Fourier coefficient of absolute
value greater than $\varepsilon$. Then there is a set $J$ of coordinates whose
complement has size at most $k$, and an assignment of signs to the coordinates outside
$J$, such that restricting $f$ to that assignment changes its mean by more than
$\varepsilon$ in absolute value.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Fourier regularity and restriction means]
\lean{FABL.isLowDegreeFourierRegular_zero_iff_forall_mean_signRestriction_eq}
\proofsource{Analysis-of-Boolean-Functions-by-Ryan-ODonnell}{pdf-ffbe9c7b3306-p147-b004}
\label{FABL.isLowDegreeFourierRegular_zero_iff_forall_mean_signRestriction_eq}
\leanok
\uses{FABL.FixedIndex, FABL.FixedSignCube, FABL.IsLowDegreeFourierRegular, FABL.IsLowDegreeFourierRegular.abs_mean_signRestriction_sub_mean_le, FABL.exists_signRestriction_mean_change_gt_of_not_isLowDegreeFourierRegular, FABL.mean, FABL.signRestriction}
\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ and $k$ be nonnegative integers, and let $f$ be a real-valued function on the
$n$-dimensional Boolean cube. Its Fourier coefficients vanish on every nonempty set of
at most $k$ coordinates if and only if, for every coordinate set $J$ and every
assignment of signs to the coordinates outside $J$ such that the complement of $J$ has
cardinality at most $k$, the mean of the resulting restriction of $f$ to the coordinates
in $J$ equals the mean of $f$ on the full cube.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Covariance and density expectation]
\lean{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.covariance_binaryFunctionOnSignCube_eq_expectation_sub_mean}
\label{FABL.ProbabilityDensity.covariance_binaryFunctionOnSignCube_eq_expectation_sub_mean}
\leanok

\difficulty{4}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer, let $\varphi$ be a probability density on $\mathbb
F_2^n$, and let $h:\{\pm1\}^n\to\{\pm1\}$. The covariance of the function on
$\{\pm1\}^n$ induced by $\varphi$ through the coordinatewise binary-to-sign bijection
with the real-valued version of $h$ equals the expectation of $h$ under $\varphi$
(evaluated after that bijection) minus the uniform mean of $h$.
\end{theorem}

F_2^n$, and let $k$ be a nonnegative integer. The covariance of the function on
$\{\pm1\}^n$ induced by $\varphi$ through the coordinatewise binary-to-sign bijection
with every Boolean function taking values in $\{\pm1\}$ and depending on at most $k$
coordinates is zero if and only if, for every such function, its expectation under
$\varphi$ after the coordinatewise bijection equals its uniform mean on $\{\pm1\}^n$.
\end{theorem}

\leanok

Let $n,k\in\mathbb N$ and let $\rho$ be a probability density on $\bbr_2^n$. Every
nonempty coordinate set of size at most $k$ has Fourier coefficient zero for the
function obtained by expressing $\rho$ on the sign cube if and only if, for every
sign-valued function $h$ on the sign cube that depends on at most $k$ coordinates, the
expectation of $h$ under $\rho$ (transported from the sign cube to the binary cube by
the coordinatewise binary-to-sign bijection) equals the uniform mean of $h$ on the sign
cube.
\end{theorem}
